title: Linking manifests and browser metadata
learningObjectives: Explain linking manifests and browser metadata and apply accurate document metadata or print structure.

understand.concept: A web app manifest is a JSON file linked using rel=manifest. It can define the application's name, short_name, start_url, display mode, theme colour, background colour, and icon resources. Browser metadata also includes theme-color and related document settings.
understand.whyItMatters: Manifest paths and icons must exist and be served with appropriate content types. A manifest does not by itself make an app fully installable or offline; service worker and platform requirements also matter.
understand.analogy: The manifest is a small identity and launch card that tells a supporting browser how the web app should be presented.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; browser metadata and search/social platform processing are governed by their respective specifications and policies.

explain.narrative: The page sets a browser theme colour and links its manifest. The manifest itself must be a valid JSON file at the linked path.

examples.explanation: The page sets a browser theme colour and links its manifest. The manifest itself must be a valid JSON file at the linked path.
examples.expectedOutput: A valid HTML head or print-style example demonstrating the topic.

practise.guidedTask: Inspect a web app manifest and verify its name, icons, start_url, display, and theme colours. Explain which features require additional implementation.
practise.independentTask: Prepare metadata or print styles for a sample course page. Verify paths, content accuracy, language declarations, and the print result.
hints: Use absolute URLs where metadata requires them.
Do not invent structured data claims.
Keep the visible page consistent with metadata.

practice.starterCode:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"><title>Linking manifests and browser metadata</title></head><body>
<head><meta name='theme-color' content='#245b48'><link rel='manifest' href='/manifest.webmanifest'></head>
</body></html>

questions.prompt: Which rel value links a web app manifest?
questions.explanation: rel=manifest links the web app manifest resource.

questions.prompt: What is the most important rule for page metadata?
options: It must accurately describe the actual page
It should contain as many keywords as possible
It can claim features not present on the page
questions.answer: It must accurately describe the actual page
questions.explanation: Metadata should be accurate, consistent, and not misleading.
